Rashi on Eruvin 3a:1:1.hebrew: לא תיהני ליה אמלתרא - לאכשורי גובהו יותר מכ', לקמן מפרש מאי אמלתרא והיכא תני דמהניא:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:1:1.english: The amaltara should not help it - to validate its height [when it is] more than twenty [cubits]. Below [the Gemara] explains what amaltara is, and where [the mishna] teaches that it helps.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:1:2.english: Of gall-nut - A tree on which galls grow; they are afatzim [oak galls], and in the vernacular [Old French]: gales.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:1.english: Why then did Rabbi Ile'a say, etc.? - Now [the Gemara] is bringing its rebuttal to a conclusion — [demonstrating] that we have found that the amaltara is effective according to Rav. But at the outset [the Gemara] did not allow [the questioner] to complete his statement until it had refuted his objection.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:2.hebrew: רחבה ד' - אם היתה קורה רחבה ד' טפחים, אע"פ שהיא דקה ואינה חזקה לקבל אריח, כשירה. והא דתנן במתניתין (לקמן עירובין ד' יג:) בריאה כדי לקבל אריח, כשאינה רחבה ד' טפחים קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:2.english: Wide four [handbreadths] - If the beam was four handbreadths wide, even though it is thin and not strong enough to hold a half-brick, it is valid. And that which we learned in the Mishna (later, Eruvin 13b): "[the beam must be] sturdy enough to hold a half-brick" — that is speaking when it is not four handbreadths wide.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:4:3.english: And if it has an amaltera, etc. - Rav is stating two things, and [both are] leniencies.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:6:1.english: And let it pose a difficulty for Rav - For we see here that the Rabbis did not derive [their ruling] from the Heikhal, since they enacted that the amaltara is effective.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:1.english: Remove me from here - Remove me from here, as if I had been silent and had not said this thing.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:2.hebrew: מתנייתא מי לא קשיין אהדדי - דהא תניא לעיל בהדיא מבוי שהוא גבוה מכ' יותר מפתחו של היכל, אלמא רבנן מהתם גמרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:2.english: Do the baraitot not contradict each other? - For it is explicitly taught above [in a baraita]: an alleyway that is more than twenty [cubits] high exceeds the entrance of the Heikhal. Hence, the Rabbis derive [the measure of twenty cubits] from there.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:3.hebrew: תנאי היא - תנא דלעיל דסבירא ליה דרבנן מהיכל גמרי, ואמלתרא לא מהניא, והאי תנא דאמלתרא סבר לאו מהיכל גמרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:3.english: It is a tannaitic dispute - The tanna cited above holds that the Rabbis derive [the measurement] from the Heikhal, and the amaltara does not help [to lower it], whereas this tanna who [permits] the amaltara holds that they do not derive [it] from the Heikhal.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:7:4.english: For me too, it is a dispute [between Tannaim] - And I say in accordance with the Tanna cited above.

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:1.english: Without Rav - If Rav had not explained the first mishna and derived from it that the Rabbis derived [the measurement] from the Heikhal [Temple sanctuary].

Rashi on Eruvin 3a:8:2.english: The mishnayot do not contradict each other - For both that mishna and this mishna [apply to the case of an] amlatera.
